title: The Judges of the Diaspora
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: This designation refers to Karna in Sanhedrin 17b. It also appears in Bava Batra 51a, 70a, 70b and 100a. Hyman reports that Rashbam explains in all these places that the judges were Shmuel and Karna, citing Sanhedrin 17b; Hyman concludes that this was undoubtedly his reading there. Hyman argues that although that passage calls Rav and Shmuel “our Rabbis in Babylonia,” this refers to the period after Rav Shila’s death, when they founded two academies and were called “our Rabbis in Babylonia.” Before that, Shmuel and Karna were simply “the judges of the Diaspora.” He considers this clear.

notes.text: Karna is the designation’s referent in the checked Sanhedrin text. Rashbam’s Shmuel-and-Karna reading and the two-academy chronology are Hyman’s reported reading and explanation.

The consulted Sanhedrin 17b identifies the judges of the Diaspora as Karna. Rashbam on Bava Batra 51a names Shmuel and Karna. Hyman’s inference about Rashbam’s reading and his two-academy chronology remain his argument; its asserted confidence is preserved.
